'''Karl-Hermann Steinberg''' (22 June 1941 – 17 October 2021<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gläser|first=Roger|date=October 27, 2021|title=Trauer um Prof. Dr. Karl-Hermann Steinberg|url=https://www.uni-leipzig.de/newsdetail/artikel/trauer-um-prof-dr-karl-hermann-steinberg-2021-10-27/|website=Universität Leipzig}}</ref>) was an eminent [[Germany|German]] [[university lecturer]] in [[Chemistry]] who became a [[politician]] ([[Christian Democratic Union (East Germany)|CDU]])<ref name=LATK-HS>{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-03-22-me-1157-story.html|title=E. German Spends Historic Day at UCI|publisher=[[Los Angeles Times]]|author=Bob Schwartz|work=[[Orange County, California|Orange County]] focus|language= English|date=22 March 1990|access-date=22 February 2015}}</ref> and briefly, in [[Die Wende|1990]] a deputy party chairman, and a Government Minister during the final months of the [[German Democratic Republic]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenK-HS>{{cite web|url=http://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=3390|author1= [[Helmut Müller-Enbergs]] |title=Steinberg, Karl-Hermann * 22.6.1941 Stellv. Vorsitzender der CDU, Minister für Umwelt- u. Naturschutz, Energie u. Reaktorsicherheit.|publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |language= German|accessdate= 22 February 2015}}</ref>

==Life==

===Early years===
Steinberg was born at the height of the [[Second World War|war]] in what had been a spa town in the south of what was then the central part of Germany. His father was a clerical worker. The war ended shortly before he was four, and the entire region became the [[Soviet occupation zone]] in what had formerly been Germany. When he was eight, in October 1949, the establishment of the [[German Democratic Republic]] formally put an end to [[Soviet Military Administration in Germany|Soviet Military Administration]], substituting a stand-alone German state with its constitutional arrangements closely modeled on the [[Soviet Union]] and its [[Group of Soviet Forces in Germany|governing class]] supported by Moscow. Steinberg [[Abitur|successfully concluded]] his schooling and in 1954 joined the [[Free German Youth|Free German Youth (FDJ / ''Freie Deutsche Jugend'')]], which was in effect the "youth wing" of the young country's ''{{lang|de|[[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|Sozialistische Einheitspartei Deutschlands]]}}''.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenK-HS/> Later, in 1959, he joined the [[Christian Democratic Union (East Germany)|Christian Democratic Union]] which under the constitutional arrangements then in force was one of several [[Bloc party (politics)|bloc parties]] operated under the control of the SED (party) through an administrative structure called the [[National Front (East Germany)|National Front]]. In 1964 he also joined the ''{{lang|de|[[Free German Trade Union Federation|Freier Deutscher Gewerkschaftsbund]]}}''. Between 1959 and 1964 he studied at the {{Interlanguage link|Leuna-Merseburg Technical Academy|de|3=Technische Hochschule Leuna-Merseburg}}, graduating with a degree in [[Chemistry]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenK-HS/>

===Academic career===
Steinberg remained at Leuna from 1964 till 1970, working as a research assistant. He received his doctorate in 1968 for a dissertation on [[surface science]] and catalysis (''{{lang|de|Oberflächenchemie u. Katalyse}}''). From 1971, still at Leuna, he was working as a research lecturer. Between 1974 and 1977 he worked nearby as a research chemist at [[Volkseigener Betrieb|VEB]] {{Interlanguage link|Leunawerke|de}}, originally a [[BASF]] plant and after 1949 East Germany's largest chemicals plant.   He nevertheless retained his connections with the academic world, achieving his [[habilitation]] (a further academic qualification) in 1976. In 1977 he was appointed to a full lectureship. In 1982 he moved to the [[Leipzig University|Karl Marx University of Leipzig]] (as it was then known) as Professor for Technical Chemistry.<ref name= BiographischeDatenbankenK-HS/><ref name=UniZeitungK-HS>{{cite web|url=https://www.archiv.uni-leipzig.de/wp-content/uploads/unizeitung/Jahrgang%201986/klein_22_UZ_30%2005%201986.pdf|author=Petra Schink|title=Es ist ein gutes Gefühl, Nützliches vollbracht zu haben: Prof. Dr. Steinberg (CDU), Sektion Chemie, kandidiert für die Volkskammer|publisher=Universitätsarchiv Leipzig|work=UZ - Universitätszeitung: Organ der Kreisleitung der SED|date=30 May 1986|page=4|volume=UZ22|accessdate=22 February 2015|archive-date=22 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150222181550/https://www.archiv.uni-leipzig.de/wp-content/uploads/unizeitung/Jahrgang%201986/klein_22_UZ_30%2005%201986.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Politics===
Although the [[German Democratic Republic]] had been formally founded only in 1949, the basis for a return to one-party government had been established in April 1946, with the [[Merger of the KPD and SPD into the Socialist Unity Party of Germany|contentious merger]] of the old [[Communist Party of Germany|Communist Party]] with the Moderate-left [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|SPD]]. Since [[1950 East German general election|1950 elections]] had been choreographed to ensure that approximately 99% of the vote went to the ruling [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|SED]], but the [[Bloc party (politics)|bloc parties]] also received a fixed quota of seats in the national legislative assembly ''[[People's Chamber|Volkskammer]]'', and from 1971 till October 1990 Karl-Hermann Steinberg served as a member of the assembly.<ref name=UniZeitungK-HS/>  He was also, from 1970, a member of the [[Christian Democratic Union (East Germany)|CDU]]'s regional committee for [[Merseburg]] and of the party's district committee for [[Halle (Bezirk)|Halle]].<ref name= BiographischeDatenbankenK-HS/>

Nationally, Steinberg became a deputy president of the [[Christian Democratic Union (East Germany)|CDU]] in December 1989, a month after the [[Die Wende|breach]] of the [[Berlin Wall]] had set in motion a series of events which would lead to [[German reunification|reunification]] in October 1990.<ref name=LATK-HS/>  He serve from 1989 as a Deputy Minister for Heavy Industry. After the [[1990 East German general election|1990 election]] he served from April 1990 as Minister for Protection of the Environment and Nature, for Reactor Safety and for Energy under [[Lothar de Maizière]].   His critical responsibilities included decommissioning principal sources of pollution in the old East German chemicals industry and the closure of the [[Greifswald Nuclear Power Plant]].   He was also mandated to negotiate with [[West Germany]] for an "Environment Union" between the two Germanys. along with gas and electricity power supply agreements.<ref name= BiographischeDatenbankenK-HS/> Steinberger's national ministerial responsibilities ended in October 1990 when the agreements covering [[German reunification]] ended to the separate East German government.

In October 1990, he briefly served as the [[Landesbevollmächtigter|interim head of government]] of the newly re-established state of [[Saxony-Anhalt]] until the election of [[List of Minister-Presidents of Saxony-Anhalt|Minister-President]] [[Gerd Gies]].

===Science and industry===
After his period in national politics came to an end Steinberg returned to [[Leipzig University]]. Before the end of 1991 he had set himself up as a self-employed business consultant. Soon after this he became Research Director with [[Preussag|Preussag AG]], and took on a project to develop a technology or system to reduce the high level of [[CO2|CO<sub>2</sub>]] emitted by the company. He began work on a system using laboratory-cultured [[Chlorella]] ([[Algae|MicroAlgae]]).   Three years later research had progressed to the point at which a pilot project was ready for launch, but now [[Preussag|Preussag AG]] mutated into a [[TUI Group|Travel and tourism]] business, which meant that it was no longer interested in the project Steinberg had been conducting for it. Steinberg continued to believe in the technology, however, and established a stand-alone business with the [[bioreactor]] technology and himself in charge.<ref name= BiographischeDatenbankenK-HS/>

He sought and found support both in the private sector and from the {{Interlanguage link|regional government|de|3=Landesregierung von Sachsen-Anhalt}} of [[Saxony-Anhalt]], which invited him to establish his business in [[Klötze]], some 20&nbsp;km to the north-east of [[Wolfsburg]].   Early production was not without set-backs, and it became clear that the business would need to be developed with the commercial backing of a larger corporation, as a result of which, in 2008, the business moved in under the corporate roof of [[Roquette Frères]], a privately owned multi-national diversified manufacturing conglomerate with a specialism in starches and products in the medicines, cosmetics and foodstuffs sectors.<ref name=MittDeut>{{cite web |url=http://www.mz-web.de/wirtschaft/sachsen-anhalt-mikroalgen-aus-der-altmark-mindern-co2-aufkommen,20642182,18352130.html|author= Klaus-Peter Voigt |title= Mikroalgen aus der Altmark mindern CO2-Aufkommen |publisher= [[Mitteldeutsche Zeitung]], [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]]|date= 15 August 2008 |accessdate=22 February 2015}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Steinberg's awards and honours have included the [[Patriotic Order of Merit]] in Bronze (1985) and the [[Banner of Labor]].
